evals.name: add-jwt-refresh-rotation
evals.prompt: Este servicio solo tiene un access token de JWT que dura para siempre, necesito agregar refresh tokens con rotación para que expire y se pueda renovar.
evals.expected_output: Adds a refresh token flow on top of the existing access-token-only setup: a refresh token DTO/endpoint, refresh token signing, and rotation/invalidation tracked in Redis (flagging that Redis needs to be added, since the current docker-compose only has postgres). Reuses the existing AuthenticationService and User entity rather than replacing them. Does not introduce session-based auth or API keys, since neither was asked for.
assertions: Recognizes the existing access-token-only JWT setup and extends it rather than rewriting auth from scratch
Adds refresh token generation, storage, and rotation grounded in references/jwt-authentication.md
Flags that Redis is not yet part of this project's stack (docker-compose only has postgres) instead of silently assuming it's available
Does not add session-based auth, API keys, roles/permissions/policies, Google Sign-In, or 2FA — none of that was requested
TTL values are treated as seconds, not milliseconds

evals.name: choose-auth-pattern-cli-integration
evals.prompt: Necesito que un cronjob interno y un webhook de un partner puedan llamar a este servicio de facturación. No hay usuarios humanos todavía.
evals.expected_output: Recommends API key authentication rather than JWT or session auth, explaining why: both callers are machine clients, not interactive human sessions, and there is no user login flow to attach JWT/session state to. Implements the API key entity, hashing, and guard from references/api-key-authentication.md, scoped appropriately for a cron job vs. a partner webhook (e.g. separate keys/scopes for each).
assertions: Recommends API key authentication over JWT or session auth, with an explicit reason tied to the machine-to-machine nature of both callers
Does not implement a user sign-up/sign-in flow, since there are no human users
API keys are stored hashed, never in plain text, per references/api-key-authentication.md
Suggests separate keys/scopes per caller (cron job vs. partner webhook) rather than one shared key
Checks the boolean result of key validation before granting access

evals.name: add-rbac-authorization
evals.prompt: Quiero que solo los supervisores puedan cerrar o reasignar tickets, los agentes normales no. ¿Cómo lo implemento en NestJS?
evals.expected_output: Recommends role-based authorization (RBAC) over granular permissions or policies, since the described access model is a simple two-category split (agent vs. supervisor) with no per-action granularity or contextual/ownership rule mentioned. Implements the Role enum, Roles decorator, and RolesGuard from references/authorization-strategies.md, adding a role column to the existing User entity. Does not introduce a permissions system or policy handlers, since the described need doesn't call for that granularity.
assertions: Recommends roles (RBAC) rather than permissions or policies, with reasoning tied to the two-category access model described
Adds a role column/enum to the existing User entity instead of creating a parallel authorization model
Implements Roles decorator + RolesGuard grounded in references/authorization-strategies.md
Does not add a full permissions or policy system unless the user's request is reinterpreted to need it
